Phân loại KHÔNG BAO GIỜ dựa vào chuỗi trạng thái tổng quát của GitHub (chưa từng được chứng minh thật cho một PR đã đóng/đã merge, per S1) — chỉ dựa hai trường tự-nó-đã-rõ-nghĩa: đã-đóng-chưa (đúng/sai) và đã-merge-lúc-nào (có/không dấu thời gian). Ba nhánh: còn mở (không việc gì), đã merge (chỉ thông tin, không tự đổi trạng thái cục bộ — kể cả khi merge diễn ra thẳng trên GitHub bỏ qua `approve --github`, đối chiếu lại nằm ngoài phạm vi), đã đóng không merge (nêu số PR, hướng dẫn gọi `fgos reject` — không tự động gọi thay). Dưới MỌI nhánh, kể cả nhánh lỗi gọi GitHub: không sự kiện nào được ghi, không friction nào — một PR bị đóng trên GitHub không tự nó là một hành động duyệt hay từ chối, y hệt nguyên tắc `reject` không tự động (RUL22 (reject không bao giờ đảo lịch sử)) áp cho hướng ngược lại.
- **RUL45 (báo việc-phát-hiện của trợ lý: đúng một lần mỗi lượt, fail-safe, không niềm tin đặc biệt, có trần + chống trùng).** Kênh báo-cáo mô tả ở "Báo việc-phát-hiện từ trợ lý" (trên) giữ nguyên tắc một-người-ghi (chỉ runner ghi work-state, trợ lý không bao giờ được phép) trong khi vẫn cho trợ lý một đường DỮ LIỆU để lộ ra việc mới: (1) việc tách báo-cáo khỏi output chạy đúng MỘT LẦN cho mỗi lượt dispatch, tại thời điểm kết thúc (thành đề xuất/chấm-trượt/quá-giờ/hỏng) — không lặp lại giữa các lần thử nội bộ của cùng lượt, nên một báo-cáo lộ ra sớm rồi lặp lại ở lần thử sau trong CÙNG lượt không bao giờ tạo hai bản; (2) một báo-cáo hỏng-hình không bao giờ đổi kết cục của chính lượt dispatch — bị bỏ qua âm thầm, không throw; (3) item tạo ra từ báo-cáo vào hệ với KHÔNG niềm tin đặc biệt nào — cùng giai đoạn đầu vào, cùng vòng xét-lại như một item người tự khai; (4) một lượt dispatch chỉ hành động trên tối đa một số báo-cáo GIỚI HẠN, phần dư bị bỏ qua có ghi lại (S10, review-fix P2 — chặn một trợ lý bất thường sinh vô hạn item); (5) một báo-cáo đã được ghi nhận trước đó (khớp dòng dõi phát-hiện + tên việc, không phân biệt hoa/thường/khoảng trắng) không tạo item thứ hai — dù lặp trong CÙNG output hay tái xuất hiện ở một lượt dispatch SAU của cùng item nguồn (S10, review-fix P2 — chặn trùng lặp khi báo-cáo bị gửi lại) — hai tên việc THẬT SỰ khác nhau vẫn cả hai được tạo (per work-graph-intelligence S2b / 8cf7effe, S10 / 7bbe6315). **Bảo đảm giao-nhận (S11, review-fix P3).** Kênh là cố-gắng-tối-đa, TỐI-ĐA-MỘT-LẦN — không phải ít-nhất-một-lần: một báo-cáo mất giữa lúc phân tích và lúc ghi xong (vd runner chết đột ngột) không được phục hồi, không có đối-soát-lại nào đọc lại output đã lưu để dựng lại báo-cáo đã mất — chấp nhận CÓ CHỦ Ý cho một kênh tư vấn phi-chặn, không phải một hàng đợi đáng tin cậy. **Ranh giới tin cậy (S11, review-fix P3).** Tên/mô tả trong một báo-cáo là văn bản KHÔNG ĐÁNG TIN do trợ lý tự soạn; item tạo ra nạp thẳng văn bản đó vào prompt của worker nghiên-cứu ở stage `discovery` — mặt tiếp xúc thứ hai (sau chính trợ lý) nơi văn bản không đáng tin chạm một model sẽ sinh lệnh chạy được. Giảm nhẹ hiện có: `verify` KHÔNG BAO GIỜ do trợ lý đặt trực tiếp (luôn qua placeholder rồi được gán lại ở vòng nghiên-cứu/làm-rõ, và một đề xuất verify còn phải qua một vòng kiểm cú pháp độc lập trước khi được ghi) nên văn bản đó không thể tự nó thành một lệnh shell; item không mang niềm tin đặc biệt, đi qua đúng vòng xét-lại như mọi item khác. Một cửa xét-duyệt-người bắt buộc trước dispatch tự động của item runner-tự-tạo được cân nhắc nhưng CHƯA XÂY (đổi thiết kế lớn hơn phạm vi vá P3) — xem decision ADR0013 (kênh báo-cáo-không-ghi cho discovered-from — worker phát khối rào fgos-discovered, runner đọc và tự ghi). **Kỷ luật ghi log (S11, review-fix P3).** Tên việc trong một báo-cáo — văn bản KHÔNG ĐÁNG TIN — được CHUẨN HOÁ (gộp khoảng trắng/xuống dòng, cắt độ dài) trước khi đưa vào bất kỳ dòng log nào của kênh này; một tên việc mang ký tự xuống dòng không thể giả-mạo thêm dòng log. Việc chuẩn hoá này CHỈ áp dụng cho bản ghi log — tên việc ĐẦY ĐỦ, nguyên văn vẫn được lưu trên item tạo ra, không bị cắt hay đổi.

- **RUL46 (lớp hướng dẫn không bao giờ tự áp cạnh chuyển-trạng-thái — chỉ engine mới được).** Skill hướng dẫn giai đoạn (làm-rõ/chia-việc/thẩm-định) chỉ SÀNG LỌC câu hỏi, GHI giả định, và PHÁN xong-hay-chưa trong phạm vi phán đoán của chính nó — cạnh chuyển stage thật sự luôn đi qua verb máy của engine, không bao giờ do chính skill tự gọi hay tự suy ra kết quả (per p50-workflow-induct, cùng stance RUL42 (stance trí-tuệ-giao-việc — picker cơ học vĩnh viễn, trí tuệ vào qua đúng hai cửa)).
- **RUL47 (cổng chờ-người của lớp hướng dẫn không bao giờ tự trả lời).** Khi engine tự phán một item chưa đủ rõ/chưa đủ khả thi (cổng chờ-người), lớp hướng dẫn luôn escalate ra ngoài phiên và chờ người quyết — không bao giờ tự đưa ra câu trả lời thay người, kể cả khi câu hỏi có vẻ hiển nhiên (per p50-workflow-induct, mở rộng RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau)/RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) sang lớp hướng dẫn).
- **RUL48 ([phần `--config` của `fgos-runner` ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each): cờ đã bỏ, `fgos discover` giữ nguyên] cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước).** `fgos discover` và `fgos-runner` đều giải đường cấu hình mặc định (không kèm `--config`) và, nếu đường đó chưa tồn tại, tự viết một bản mặc định (cùng hình dạng với cấu hình dogfood của chính repo — model light/standard/heavy, `timeoutMs`, khối `parallel`) trước khi nạp — không còn báo lỗi "không đọc được cấu hình" ngay từ bước đầu tiên của vòng làm-rõ. Việc tự sinh này LUÔN kèm một dòng thông báo (tên file + executor được chọn) để người vận hành biết ngay cấu hình vừa được tạo, không âm thầm. Một `--config <path>` TƯỜNG MINH trỏ vào đường vắng mặt KHÔNG BAO GIỜ được tự sinh thay — vẫn báo lỗi ngay như trước, vì một đường dẫn người tự chỉ định là chủ đích, không phải "chưa từng cấu hình" (per D 38f7e0b8).
- **RUL48b (bản mặc định tự sinh dò trợ lý sẵn có trên máy thay vì luôn giả định `claude` — STR82).** Trước khi viết bản mặc định của RUL48 (cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước), việc tự sinh dò xem máy có sẵn trợ lý nào trong một danh sách trợ lý nhận diện được (`claude`, `codex`, mở rộng được) — dò sự HIỆN DIỆN thôi, không gọi/chạy thử trợ lý đó. Tìm thấy `claude` → executor viết ra y hệt bản mặc định trước STR82 (không đổi hành vi trên máy đã có Claude Code). Không thấy `claude` nhưng thấy một trợ lý nhận diện được khác (vd `codex`) mà runner CHƯA có mẫu lệnh gọi đã kiểm chứng cho trợ lý đó, hoặc không thấy trợ lý nhận diện được nào → executor viết ra một lệnh placeholder tự-báo-lỗi (tên lệnh nêu rõ ngay nguyên nhân: không tìm thấy trợ lý, hay tìm thấy trợ lý X nhưng chưa có mẫu lệnh) thay vì đoán một mẫu lệnh gọi chưa kiểm chứng — để người vận hành gặp lỗi rõ ràng NGAY lúc cấu hình được tạo, thay vì đâm tường muộn ở bước dispatch thật với thông báo "command not found" khó hiểu. Dòng thông báo tự sinh của RUL48 (cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước) luôn nêu rõ trợ lý nào được dò thấy (hay không thấy trợ lý nào) và executor nào vừa được viết. Nhánh nạp cấu hình đã có sẵn (merge khoá mặc định còn thiếu) không đổi — việc dò chỉ chạy khi tự sinh bản MỚI (per D1bc96509).
- **RUL49 (khóa hoạt động cây chính chặn CỨNG, không phải cảnh báo — canh MỌI commit trần, không riêng gì verb fgOS).** Cơ chế mô tả ở "Khóa hoạt động cây chính" trên chặn ở tầng git, trước khi bất kỳ commit nào chạm cây chính — không phải một guard trong `bin/fgos.mjs`, nên không thể bị vòng qua bằng cách gọi git trực tiếp thay vì qua verb fgOS (đúng lỗ hổng đã biết của "Bảo vệ approve khỏi lồng phiên" trên, vốn chỉ canh MỘT verb và chỉ canh phiên đã đăng ký). Đèn hoạt động dùng đúng một danh tính (biến môi trường phiên trợ lý khi có, tổ tiên tiến trình gần khi không) để phân biệt "chính phiên này tiếp tục" khỏi "một phiên khác đang hoạt động" — cùng danh tính không bao giờ tự chặn chính mình (per STR65). Mutex `main-checkout` thì không nhận diện ai: nó là kernel lock, writer fgOS giữ qua một cửa và git con mượn qua description, không có TTL, không tự-nhận-diện theo pid.
- **RUL50 (khóa hoạt động cây chính fail-closed trên tín hiệu không đọc được).** Khi nội dung đèn không phân tích được thì chỉ là gợi ý hỏng (cảnh báo rồi cho qua); còn khi khóa `main-checkout` đang bị giữ mà commit không phải con mượn, commit bị từ chối — không bao giờ được coi là "cây đang rảnh". Kernel lock chỉ có hai trạng thái `held`/`free`, không còn trạng thái mơ hồ. Đây là lựa chọn CHỦ Ý ưu tiên an toàn hơn sẵn sàng, khác với "Bảo vệ approve khỏi lồng phiên"'s `isMainWorktree` (fail-open trên trường hợp mơ hồ) — hai cơ chế bảo vệ hai rủi ro khác nhau (một canh thẩm quyền FSM, một canh mất-dữ-liệu-thật đang hoạt động) nên được phép chọn khác nhau (per STR65).
- **RUL51 (repo phải có ≥1 commit trước khi runner claim bất kỳ item nào — kiểm MỘT LẦN lúc khởi động, không phải mỗi item).** `resolveRepoRoot` (site khởi động DUY NHẤT, gọi từ `main()` TRƯỚC `runOnce`) nay còn xác nhận HEAD của repo resolve được, không chỉ xác nhận repo là một repo git — cùng phạm trù lỗi `validation` với nhánh không-phải-repo-git đã có từ trước. Đây là kiểm MỘT LẦN mỗi lần `fgos-runner` khởi động, KHÔNG phải một nhánh mới trong bảng phục hồi per-item (Data Dictionary #3): trước quyết định này, một repo 0 commit khiến MỌI item đầu tiên được claim thất bại ở bước `git worktree add` (HEAD không resolve), tốn `maxRetries` lượt thử-rồi-đỗ (RUL7 (schema item mang đủ chất liệu trả lời sáu câu hỏi harness)/Data Dictionary #3) trước khi lộ ra một lỗi worktree khó truy nguyên; nay runner dừng NGAY tại khởi động với đúng nguyên nhân + cách sửa, không claim item nào, không chạm bảng phục hồi/`recovery.mjs` (per D ecfd0d1a).
- **RUL52 (luật template theo domain `coding` khớp TRƯỚC wildcard; domain lạ/vắng mặt fold về `coding` giống mọi nơi khác trong hệ — STR91).** Bảng luật của `selectTemplate` (Data Dictionary #11, RUL44 (đã xây — STR49, `src/runner/prompt-templates.mjs`)) từ STR91 có thêm một luật đứng TRƯỚC luật wildcard cuối: `domain === 'coding'` (sau khi fold) trỏ `worker-prompt-skill-pointer.txt` — giữ nguyên đủ 6 mục cố định của template mặc định (5 mục khung `# Goal`/`# Description`/`# Worktree boundary`/`# Expected proof`/`# Constraints` cộng mục kênh báo-cáo `` ```fgos-discovered``` ``), CHỈ thêm đúng một mục mới `# Agent skill`. Phép fold domain (`undefined` hoặc một chuỗi domain KHÔNG nhận diện được → `coding`) diễn ra ĐÚNG MỘT nơi — bên trong chính `selectTemplate` (không phải ở nơi gọi `buildPrompt`/`spawnWorker`, vốn luôn truyền `work.domain` thô, nguyên vẹn) — cùng phép fold-về-`coding` hệ thống đã dùng ở lớp hướng dẫn qua skill (xem "Vòng làm việc có hướng dẫn qua tầng skill trích xuất" trên: entry skill `fgos-routing` cũng fold domain vắng mặt về `coding`), không phải một luật fallback riêng của prompt template. Đường dẫn skill (`{skillPath}`, dạng `.claude/skills/<skillName>/SKILL.md`) LUÔN resolve qua sổ đăng ký domain→skill sẵn có (`getDomain`/`skillForStage`, spec Work-State "Mô hình domain", per STR89/STR90) — KHÔNG BAO GIỜ một literal hardcode — nên luật này tự hội tụ cho bất kỳ domain tương lai nào (vd `marketing`) NGAY khi domain đó khai `skillMap` riêng cho stage `executing`, không cần sửa thêm code ở đây. Một domain đã đăng ký khác `coding` (vd `synthetic`) không đi qua luật mới — vẫn rơi về wildcard, nhận `worker-prompt-default.txt` như trước STR91 (per str91-runner-skill-convergence).


- **RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao BỀN, dừng CHỈ khi có tín hiệu tường minh — str7-str8-priority-intent).** `fgos-runner --watch` lặp lại nguyên vẹn vòng đời "Một vòng --once" nhiều lượt liên tiếp, KHÔNG dừng khi frontier rỗng (khác `--once`, vốn dừng khi rỗng): một lượt vừa GHI được gì (bất kỳ giao dịch cửa-ghi nào thành công) thì lượt kế tiếp bắt đầu NGAY, không chờ; một lượt không ghi được gì thì lượt kế tiếp chờ một khoảng nghỉ mặc định (đổi được qua `--poll-ms`) trước khi thử lại. Bộ đếm cầu dao (Data Dictionary #5) dùng CHUNG một thực thể xuyên suốt MỌI lượt của một tiến trình `--watch` — khác `--once`, nơi mỗi lời gọi có cầu dao riêng — nên cầu dao KHÔNG còn trơ dưới `--watch`: một việc lỗi rải rác qua nhiều lượt vẫn cộng dồn tới trần, đúng ý nghĩa "tiến trình bền tích lũy lịch sử lỗi" của chế độ này. Một lượt gặp lỗi/dừng (halted) KHÔNG kết thúc tiến trình `--watch` — chỉ lượt đó dừng, tiến trình vẫn tiếp tục thử lượt kế tiếp; DUY NHẤT tín hiệu dừng tường minh (SIGINT/SIGTERM) kết thúc tiến trình, luôn thoát mã 0 bất kể lượt cuối cùng ra sao. Một tín hiệu dừng thứ hai (người gõ Ctrl-C lần nữa khi lượt đang chạy còn dở) buộc thoát ngay (mã 130) — lối thoát khẩn cho một lượt kẹt, không chờ nó tự xong. `--watch` không tương thích với `--dry-run` (bị chặn `validation`); `--watch --once` không lỗi — `--watch` mặc nhiên thắng, giữ đúng tiền lệ `--once` đã là cờ chấp-nhận-nhưng-không-đọc (per str7-str8-priority-intent).

- **RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb — per D2 str46-io-contract).** Mỗi lượt `--once`, và mỗi chu kỳ của `--watch`, in đúng MỘT phong bì `fgos.v1` (cùng bốn trường `contract`/`generated_at`/`data_hash`/`data` đã tả ở spec Work-State "Phong bì output") thay cho dòng chữ trần trước đây — nhưng in **liền một dòng**, không xuống dòng nhiều tầng như `fgos.mjs`: một tiến trình `--watch` sống lâu phát NHIỀU phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian, nên mỗi phong bì phải trọn trong đúng một dòng để bên đọc tách được cái này với cái kia. Với `--once`, phong bì này luôn là dòng cuối cùng của kết quả. **Ba luồng output khác của `fgos-runner` KHÔNG đổi, nằm ngoài phong bì này có chủ đích:** (1) tiến trình dò-xét từng bước bên trong một lượt (gặt-lại, nhận việc, phán làm-rõ/chia-việc, đuôi kết quả proof, thử lại, dừng) tiếp tục in thẳng ra console y nguyên như trước — luồng này thuộc "Ghi lại output của trợ lý sau mỗi lượt dispatch"/"Xem live output worker khi đang chạy" đã tả trên, một tính năng tách bạch không đụng tới; (2) bản ghi cục bộ mỗi việc (`.fgos/logs/<id>.log`) không đổi; (3) dòng xác nhận đã dừng khi nhận tín hiệu dừng tường minh (RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao bền, dừng chỉ khi có tín hiệu tường minh)) vẫn là chữ trần, không bọc phong bì — đây là một dòng vòng-đời-tiến-trình, không phải kết cục của một lượt việc. - **RUL65b (Provider Capacity Rotator slice 1 — account selection là runtime capacity, không phải placement/fallback).** Khi một Assignment Run đã qua admission và executor thắng cuộc là `kind:"agent"` out-of-process cho provider có inventory global (slice 1: `openai-codex`), runner acquire đúng một account lease dưới lock global trước launch; `dispatch-plan.json` chỉ ghi requirement, không bao giờ ghi selected account trước admission. Ranking cố định: `openLeases` tăng dần, rồi `lastSelectedAt` tăng dần, rồi `stableHash(seed, accountId)`; sticky assignment chỉ được giữ nếu account vẫn present, healthy, non-quarantined. Lease sống theo Run lifetime và chỉ reclaim khi có proof PID-dead/run-dead, không bao giờ vì elapsed TTL. `kind:"tool"`/MCP executors (ví dụ GitNexus) bypass rotator bằng discriminator hiện hữu, dù cùng provider label.

  Selection evidence là Run-owned (`provider-capacity-selection.json`, effective execution contract/evidence) và chỉ được persist dạng redacted: provider, account id/label, lease owner, reason codes/quarantine state, `credentialProvisioned`; không persist credential home path, env values, token, `auth.json` bytes, raw digest/SHA-256. Provisioning của invocation bwrap (cli-spawn và herdr-spawn) dùng selected account `credentialSource` để copy vào private home trước spawn — kind `codex-home` copy `auth.json` vào private `CODEX_HOME`, kind `home-files` (`files`: danh sách đường dẫn tương đối, không `..`) copy đúng các file đó vào private home của agent khác (pi, agy), owner-only, giữ exec bit của helper; inventory vẫn chỉ ở `~/.fgos/config.json`, và pane herdr confine dựa vào nó để khởi động đã đăng nhập (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §13.1, doctor `confined-pane-accounts`); mất/không đọc/copy lỗi thì fail closed trước spawn với class credential-provisioning/config, không quarantine account, không bind-mount real Codex home, và không còn dùng `FGOS_CODEX_CREDENTIAL_HOMES` hash rotation hay executor-id allowlist làm authority placement.

  Fault classifier chỉ đọc high-confidence provider stderr, adapter outcome đã biết (`paused-limit`), hoặc structured agent JSON như `stopReason`; không scan prompt/brief/report/general stdout. Quota/rate-limit quarantine account; auth/login/token quarantine dạng manual-clear; credential provisioning/config/test/confinement/work-product failure không quarantine. Chủ máy đặt quarantine tay bằng `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --until <ISO tương lai> --reason "<why>"` (quota-limit tạm thời, `detail.kind: owner`; unknown account hoặc `--until` không ở tương lai bị refuse; ghi vào state thật của máy, không theo `--dir`). Classifier cũng đọc giờ reset tuyệt đối codex in ("try again at 6:02 PM", giờ local, lần kế tiếp). Manual clear duy nhất là `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --reason "<why>"` (unknown provider/account bị refuse; non-quarantined account bị refuse trừ khi `--force`). `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` và `fgos doctor` chỉ report; doctor không auto-clear auth quarantine. `readOnlyExecutorRedirects` vẫn giữ nguyên trong slice này; không có `providerFallback`, `providerRuntimes`, `providers.<provider>.models`, six-tier runtime wiring, cross-provider fallback, hay retry loop trong rotator.

  Provider failure inside a Unit run goes to another account before another provider (decision 0058). A round that ends `provider-limit` is retried as the same executor and invocation under a fresh `-fb<n>` assignment id while another account of that executor's provider is usable (listed in the inventory, not quarantined) and fewer retries than that provider has accounts were spent on this candidate; the lease then ranks the next account as it always does. Only when no account is left does `nextCandidate` walk the capability pool, skipping provider families whose login failed in this unit and still preferring a family the sibling seats did not use. A process that exits non-zero with a dead-credential wording (`AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, e.g. pi "No API key found for openrouter.") in its last five stderr lines settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: credential`, so the account is quarantined as `auth-token`. A process that exits the same way with a used-up quota as its last words (`QUOTA_LIMIT_PATTERNS` in `provider-auth-failure.mjs`, line-start anchored after an optional `ERROR:`; measured: codex "ERROR: You’ve hit your usage limit. ... try again at 11:39 PM.", 2026-10-13) settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota`, with or without an account lease, so a headless cli-spawn round rotates and walks like a pane round; a leased account is quarantined `quota-limit` until the reset the provider printed (the existing `until`, no separate retry field), and a quota stop does not exclude the provider family. The capacity classifier reads the same wordings from the stderr tail only. Rescheduling a run whose accounts and candidates are all used up is not done here (Workflow runner, separate decision). Each attempt records `fallbackFrom.kind` (`account-rotation` or `next-candidate`).

 Đi kèm bắt buộc 3 gate, thiếu 1 trong 3 thì `gitnexus` (chỉ có `invocations:[{via:"mcp",...}]`, không `command`/`args` phẳng) vỡ ngay lúc load hoặc bị spawn nhầm:

  - **Gate B2 (chọn đúng invocation theo `via`, `resolveExecutorConfig`).** Không lấy `invocations[0]` mù — chọn ĐÚNG entry có `via:"cli"` (cơ chế DUY NHẤT `resolveExecutorConfig` thật sự dispatch), bất kể thứ tự khai trong mảng.
 - **Gate B3 (throw tường minh khi không dispatch-được, `resolveExecutorConfig`).** Khi 1 executor khai `invocations` nhưng KHÔNG entry nào `via:"cli"` (như `gitnexus`) — ném `RunnerConfigError` ngay, không bao giờ âm thầm rơi về `executor` toàn cục như thể executor đó chỉ mang metadata (khác hẳn 1 executor thật sự không khai `invocations`/`command`/`adapter`/`agentType` nào — ca đó vẫn rơi về `executor` toàn cục bình thường).

- **RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds).** An account quarantined as `auth-token` has no end time: the owner logs in again by hand and fgOS cannot see it. Instead of waiting for a person to run the clear command, a dispatch that finds **no usable account of the provider** makes one real, cheap call per such account (Codex: `codex exec`; an omp profile, a `home-files` source that lists `agent.db`: `omp -p`; a pi account directory, one that lists `auth.json`: `pi -p`; omp is tested before pi), against the account's own home, not a copy, because the owner uses that home and a renewal belongs there. A call that answers clears the lock (audited as `fgos provider-capacity probe`) and the dispatch goes on; one that does not keeps the lock and records the attempt, and no new call is made for that account within a 30 minute cooldown, however many dispatches ask. Only `auth-token` locks are probed: a quota limit ends by itself and any other manual lock is a person's decision. The call is never made while another account of the provider is usable, runs outside the state lock but inside the account lock of RUL75 (so a renewal made by fgOS cannot overlap it; an account whose lock stays busy past two minutes counts as a failed attempt), stops at the first account that answers, and a failure to probe never blocks the dispatch. A credential layout fgOS cannot name (the agy homes of Gemini) has no call, so that account stays locked for a person. The probe is passed to the dispatch by its callers; a caller that passes none changes nothing.

- **RUL75 (a rotating provider login is renewed once at the source, in a copy fgOS holds, and a login renewed inside a private home is written back).** Dispatch copies an account's login into a private home that is thrown away. pi, omp and Codex logins carry a single-use refresh token (measured for each), so a renewal that happens inside such a copy uses up the source's token on the provider's side and the new pair is lost with the home; the next renewal anywhere is refused (`invalid_grant`, the account is quarantined `auth-token`). Opt-in (the same shape as the lazy probe): a caller passes `providerCredentialRenew` (`createCredentialRenewal()`, `src/runner/dispatch/provider-credential-renewal.mjs`) to `executeAssignment`, and only then do the two halves below run; without it provisioning and removal are as before. `agent.db` is copied as a consistent SQLite snapshot (`VACUUM INTO`, write-ahead log included) whether or not a dispatch opted in, and the unlock probe knows the omp layout regardless.

  1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `<stateRoot>/locks/provider-account/<provider>/<account>.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case.

Về account: `--account` của workflow chỉ ghim cho các seat thuộc provider sở hữu account đó; các Unit không có seat nào khớp sẽ chạy bình thường không ghim và không làm hỏng workflow; `--account` không tồn tại trong bất kỳ `runner.providers.*.accounts` nào sẽ bị từ chối ngay lúc start trước khi tạo run.
- **RUL99 (Bảng mã thoát riêng biệt cho kết cục thực thi của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground`, 2026-10-15).** Các outcome kết thúc không phải `pass` của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` chuyển sang sử dụng bảng exit code xác định: `pass` = 0, `policy-refusal` = 4 (validation), `provider-limit` = 10, `execution-failure` = 11, `partial-writes` = 12, `blocked` = 13, `findings` = 14. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%.
- **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities.<cap>.prefer`.

- **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. The lock file is `<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`, so one directory reached through a symlink is one lock; a cwd that does not exist fails as `worker-spawn-fail` before any lock. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--<cwd>.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `<fgosDir>/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. Order inside one `LockScope` is enforced at acquire: a lock taken at a rank not above every rank the scope already holds throws `lock-order-violation` at once, with no trace-then-warn release.
- **RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor; llmAccounts is read for checking only, 2026-10-17).** A cell of `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` is a model, a model served by a named pool (`model@pool`), or a non-empty ordered list of those. The pool is the service provider that bills the call. A cell entry is split at its last `@`, so a model id that itself contains `@` names its pool explicitly (`claude-opus-4@20250514@vertex`); an entry without `@` is served by the pool named after the family. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it.
  Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors.
  `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>.<account>` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { <cli>: <login directory> }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning still read `runner.providers` only. Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared, `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare.
  `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the whole cell with each entry marked `used`, `fallback-same-pool` or `pending-pool-routing`, the executor and invocation, and the pool's accounts in both inventories. It leases, spawns and writes nothing.
- **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(<capability>, <rigor>)`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(<tier>, <ceiling source>)`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.

`tsk-34o5` elevates identity attestation from advisory-only (level 1) to mechanical enforcement (level 2). While `footprintDiffHits` remains advisory-only (diffs outside declared footprint flag scope creep without blocking), identity divergence (`baseCommit` ancestry mismatch or `headRef` mismatch) now triggers an immediate halt at all three chokepoints (`startupReap`, `fgos return`, `fgos approve`):
- **Typed Halt:** Divergent items are parked at `blocked` with the typed reason `attestation-mismatch`. No merge is attempted, main remains untouched, and friction evidence is logged.

- **Zero Friction on Green & In-Session:** Absent attestation events or `baseCommit: null` / `headRef: null` (in-session dispatches) return `{ ok: true, skipped: true }` without blocking. Legitimate retries on a branch reset to baseline remain green.
Level 2 targets identity divergence (e.g. `tsk-43z` worker committing straight to main or off-baseline ref rewrites) by enforcing a hard mechanical halt before any code is trusted or merged.

If deleting the shell is unpalatable to the maintainer, the smaller path is to reframe the premise: this is not an architecture boundary problem, it is a deployment bug.

- **Consequences:** The shell remains exactly as it is (a pure web view pointed at the daemon). You do not acquire local ownership. Instead, you spend your complexity budget strictly on fixing the cold-start race and the raw-bind-host bug in the launcher coordination logic.

- **Trigger:** You explicitly defer any architectural shift until a verifiable metric (e.g., user-perceived UI latency) proves that the HTTP daemon hop is an actual bottleneck for a real workflow. Until that trigger fires, no domain logic crosses into the shell.
- The lack of commits since July is misleading (e.g., the maintainer has been building out the daemon's backend specifically to unblock a massive desktop push planned for next week).

- The launcher coordination issues are structurally unfixable as long as the UI and daemon remain separate processes, making local ownership a strict technical necessity rather than an architectural choice.

**Recommendation:** The desktop shell should remain a thin client of the existing daemon for registry, rendering, and search. Its local ownership should cover window state, presentation preferences, and connection status only.

For this proposal, **local registry/render/search ownership** means genuine reimplementation in the shell: opening or maintaining registry data, managing indexing and watchers, rendering documents, or executing search independently of the daemon. I propose none of these. A daemon connection failure must produce a visible, recoverable connection failure—not silently activate a second authority.

**Magnitude:** potentially every cold start; the actual incidence of the concurrent-start race remains unknown. The ignored-failure path already imposes roughly 4.5 seconds of waiting without explaining the cause.

**Owner and cost:** the solo maintainer owns one launcher implementation and its regression tests. Desktop integration adds coverage, but should stop requiring parallel fixes to copied launcher logic.
### 2. Local ownership would create a second service implementation on an unmaintained surface

The shell has no tests, is absent from CI, has bundling disabled, and remains at `0.1.0` against workspace `0.7.6`, with no commits since July 20. These are evidence of missing maintenance coverage, not proof that desktop can never be maintained. They make a second implementation a poor present allocation of the sole maintainer’s capacity.

**Owner and cost:** this candidate adds a bounded desktop integration obligation. Local ownership adds ongoing service maintenance across three capabilities, plus whichever data lifecycle it chooses. There is no evidence supporting a credible hours-per-month estimate; the difference is in recurring responsibilities, not a defensible numeric multiplier.

**Owner and cost:** one maintainer observes and fixes the existing contention problem once. Desktop-local ownership would not remove existing callers; it would either join them or create another index to operate.
1. **Establish a desktop check in CI.** Compile the shell and exercise the launcher integration points. Its absence from current CI is an immediate maintenance blind spot.

Reopen the ownership boundary if measurements show an unacceptable limitation attributable to daemon execution or attachment after these repairs, and a local prototype demonstrates a material improvement with an explicit maintenance and data-retirement plan.

Doing nothing also has a cost: silent launcher failures, wrong-endpoint behavior, stale indexing, and unmeasured contention remain. The proposed investment is therefore **thin-client repair with a bounded maintenance contract**, not preservation of the current defects.

The CASE is a boundary question, not a feature request: should `mdview-desktop` stay a thin client of the daemon, or acquire local ownership of registry/render/search? Per Phase 4 defaults, "local ownership" is undefined by the panel and is mine to define; I define it as: *the shell independently implements one or more of {registry access, rendering, search/indexing} without going through the daemon's HTTP API*, and per the scout, this means genuine reimplementation — there is no existing shell-side library to relocate. I take the CASE's word "authority" seriously: the daemon is being asked to remain the place truth lives, not merely a service the shell happens to call today.

The scout's central finding is decisive: `mdview-desktop/src/main.rs` (144 lines) has zero domain logic — no `Engine`, `SqliteStore`, renderer, indexer, search, document cache, or command bridge. It is a native window around `WebviewUrl::External(url)`. Every piece of daemon capability growth in the last week (background indexing, short-link resolution, in-place editing with conflict detection — Sept 3-5 commits) landed for the shell automatically, for free, with zero shell-side changes, *because* it stayed thin. That is not incidental — it is the mechanism by which "authority" stays coherent: one writer, one place editing conflicts get resolved, one place the SQLite schema can change without a second consumer to keep in sync.

**One maintainer bears every ongoing cost of whatever is chosen, indefinitely.** This is the fact that makes the answer "thin" rather than "it depends on latency." If this were a team with dedicated desktop-platform ownership, a second implementation surface would be a normal cost of a differentiated product. With one maintainer, a duplicated Engine/renderer/search stack means every daemon-side change (which is happening weekly per the Sept 3-5 commits) becomes a two-sided change forever, or the two silently drift and the shell becomes stale in exactly the way "authority" was meant to prevent. Change this constraint (add a second maintainer with standing ownership of the desktop surface) and the proposal changes — local ownership becomes a legitimate investment rather than a standing tax on one person.

docs/history/windows-daemon-fixes/plan.md:30:**D3 — extract `apply_detach` into `mdview-core`, do not duplicate it.** This reverses the "duplicate it in place" instinct that would otherwise apply (mirroring D1): Discovery finding #3 makes duplication the wrong call here specifically, because `mdview-desktop` has no compile coverage anywhere in this repo's automation. If the platform-cfg detach logic is written *inside* `main.rs`, there is no way to unit-test it without compiling the whole Tauri-dependent binary — something neither this sandbox nor CI can currently do. Moving `apply_detach(cmd: &mut Command)` verbatim into a new `crates/mdview-core/src/process.rs` (workspace-covered, no GUI deps) makes it directly unit-testable by `cargo test --workspace` (mirroring the existing `apply_detach_puts_child_in_its_own_session` proof style — "detachment must be proven, not assumed," critical-pattern #3), and reduces `mdview-desktop`'s own change to a single call-before-spawn line — the smallest possible edit to the one crate nothing can currently verify by compiling. `runtime.rs` keeps `apply_detach` working via a `pub(crate) use mdview_core::process::apply_detach;` re-export, so its existing test needs zero changes. This is also exactly what `findings-architecture.md`'s P2 recommended (spawn/detach belongs one layer down, next to `daemon.rs`'s lock/health) — the environment constraint and the architecture finding point the same direction.

Four observable differences remain between desktop `ensure_daemon()` and CLI `ensure_bind()`:

1. **Cold-start serialization.** CLI gained an atomic spawn gate in `5887583`, July 16. Desktop does not use it. Its single-instance plugin initializes only after `ensure_daemon()`. Health checking substitutes loopback, but desktop URL construction does not. CLI has separate URL conversion logic. This is a concrete code difference; native WebView behavior for that URL across operating systems remains untested here.

**Does it settle Phase 8's "What Stays Yours"?** Yes, for the shell — and it settles it by *removing* the shell from "yours" `[high]`. From my memory of explanation.md, that question asked which parts of mdview are built for them versus for others; the answer here is that the rendering-plus-links path is theirs, the desktop shell is not. This assumes Intraday and EOD share a single temporal schedule where standard DAG blocking is valid. They do not. Intraday *must* read a previous session's data (hence the 7-day lookback). Therefore, the read cannot be resolved by standard same-date `AssetRunner` DAG edges. The System Shaper's primary mechanism is structurally incompatible with the domain's timing.

**Priors I am applying, stated up front:** I weight explicit data dependencies and operational safety over code-level structural DRYness (Don't Repeat Yourself), primarily because the repository is only a month old (83 commits). The domain boundaries between what EOD needs and what Intraday needs are still settling (e.g., EOD adding a breadth gate that Intraday bypasses). When a system is this young, structural abstraction often ossifies the wrong boundaries; I am prioritizing interventions that make runtime failures obvious over interventions that make the code cleaner. I define "difficult to evolve" not as "typing takes too long," but as "changing one thing unpredictably breaks another."

Why it is credible here: If you build a new pluggable pipeline abstraction, Intraday will still silently read EOD's lake paths and EOD will still eat Intraday's alert cap. The friction in evolution is coming from runtime side-effects, not from the structure of the `AssetRunner` or the domain functions (which are successfully tolerating drift via defaults like `pct_sectors_leading=None`).

**One alternative I tried and abandoned:** Decoupling by duplicating the shared domain functions (like `evaluate_buy_gate`) so each pipeline has its own completely isolated copy, preventing one pipeline's new requirement from forcing a bypass in the other. I dropped it because the codebase is currently handling this drift gracefully (`_gate_breadth` explicitly records the bypass). The shared domain functions aren't the acute danger right now; the invisible data dependencies are.

2. If the alert cap bleeding is actually an intentional business rule (e.g., "never send more than N alerts a day across the entire firm, regardless of source"), then my premise about state coupling is a misunderstanding of the domain.

"Difficult" means a change in one pipeline can alter the other's decisions without a declared dependency or a failing test, leaving the sole maintainer to discover and reconcile the consequences. Success means those changes become locally testable and independently deployable, with useful stopping points.

This proposal assumes there is room for bounded corrective releases while the existing jobs continue operating. It does not assume an incident, a failure frequency, or an urgency level. The lead advisor's sole-maintainer interpretation is the operational premise.

The scout traces the breadth-gate divergence to `235d05d`. Intraday's gate invocation (`src/vnflow/application/signals/signal_engine_intraday.py:122`) omits breadth, and the shared rule (`src/vnflow/domain/analytics/signal_rules.py:248`) explicitly passes unavailable breadth. The bypass is recorded in reasons, but it is not enforced as a contract failure.

*Magnitude:* every intraday buy evaluation using this invocation bypasses that gate. This does **not** mean every resulting buy is wrong: other gates still apply, and intentional exemption remains unresolved. A resulting Telegram notification, however, cannot be undone by reverting Python code; a recipient may already have acted.

*Cheapest mitigation:* make breadth policy explicit at the application boundary: either required with a value and source session, or deliberately exempt with a named reason. Missing data must not implicitly select exemption. Preserve the existing behavior initially as a visibly declared compatibility exemption; activating required breadth is a separate policy decision for the maintainer, not an architectural inference.

Each release must remain useful if work stops there. There is no dual-write interval, historical rewrite, or second engine to retire. Reader rollback is a code revert; already emitted signals and alerts remain historical effects and must not be automatically replayed.
*Operational cost:* one implementation remains on call. The maintainer does not inherit two execution systems or a migration reconciliation queue.

*Magnitude:* with intraday cap C, intraday sends I, and same-date EOD sends E, available capacity is currently `max(0, C − I − E)` instead of `max(0, C − I)`. EOD execution during the session can consume the entire remaining allowance. This is a live code path, not proof it has occurred.

*Magnitude:* one incompatible partition can invalidate the aggregate regime or sector read for that poll, potentially affecting every evaluated symbol. The mixed-schema failure remains an exposure, not a reproduced production incident.

Estimated implementation budget: **4–7 focused maintainer days**, assuming the existing repository interfaces and strategy identity support these changes. This is a planning estimate, not measured throughput.

The no-build path retains the current bypass, contamination, and context-loss exposures, plus manual discovery cost. No incident rate is available to price that cost honestly. This candidate trades that unbounded investigative burden for several finite changes that remain valuable even if the maintainer never undertakes a larger restructure.

**Which option this resolves to:** C — reframe — but not because A and B are unavailable; because the scout report falsifies the premise both A and B share. A ("separate pipelines, shared contracts") and B ("one pluggable abstraction") both assume the difficulty lives at the *execution-graph* level — that the two pipelines either need to be pulled apart with a contract in between, or fused into one engine. The report found that a shared engine (`AssetRunner`) already runs both `EOD_ASSET_SPECS` and `INTRADAY_ASSET_SPECS` through one topo-sort/materialize/check path, and that domain logic (`evaluate_buy_gate`, `score_money_flow`, `dispatch_alerts`) is already shared, not duplicated. B is a proposal to build something that exists. A is a proposal to formalize a split that isn't where the drift is. The real drift is in four specific, named seams beneath that shared engine, and none of them are fixed by re-architecting the pipeline boundary.

Every future addition that pulls a value from one pipeline's context into the other's (which is precisely what the 2026-07-05 audit is about to ask for — ATR entry planning and continuous RVOL scoring for intraday, both already produced by EOD) now costs more up front: it has to be declared as a dependency, or explicitly marked as an intentional bypass with a test, rather than just read or defaulted. I am proposing to slow down exactly the work that is already scheduled next. If the maintainer's actual complaint is "changes take too long" rather than "changes silently break the other side," this proposal makes their felt problem worse, not better.

**LOW — `--plan` path-resolution basis diverges from sibling `run --file` when `--dir` is used, untested.** `bin/fgos.mjs`'s `run` branch resolves `--file` eagerly against `process.cwd()` (`path.resolve(process.cwd(), filePath)`, `bin/fgos.mjs:3122`) before the use-case ever sees it. `launch-master-loop`'s `--plan` is instead passed raw into `launchMasterLoopUseCase`, and `assertPlanPathExists` resolves it against `ctx.cwd` (`repoRootForCoordination`) inside `launch-master-loop.mjs:53`. When `--dir` is omitted (the only case any test exercises), `repoRootForCoordination === process.cwd()` and the two behave identically — this is not observable in the current test suite. When `--dir` names a *different* main checkout, the two sub-verbs would resolve a relative path against different bases (`run` against the invoking shell's cwd, `launch-master-loop` against the target repo root). Neither behavior is obviously wrong (arguably resolving against the target repo root is more correct for a repo-relative plan path), but it's an unannounced divergence from the sibling convention and has zero test coverage either way. Smallest fix direction: either resolve `--plan` the same way `--file` is resolved (against `process.cwd()`, for consistency) in `bin/fgos.mjs`, or add one test exercising `--dir` + a relative `--plan` to lock in the intended behavior. Does not block this cell — R4's "bad file path" acceptance is satisfied for the untested-`--dir` case, and this is a pre-existing gap shared with `run --file` (which also has no `--dir` test).

Sort: a deterministic topological sort (Kahn). A node is ready when all its predecessors have been emitted. The sort repeatedly emits the ready node with the smallest key (`ts`, `origin`, `stream`, `seq`), compared field by field as bytes. The keys sit inside the hashed bytes and are unique per event, so no tie remains and no engine-dependent comparator is involved. No pairwise comparator that mixes causality and timestamps is used anywhere. The model check showed that such a comparator can be cyclic (C3), and it ran this sort 36,864 times with one result per case (section 23.1).

Unix uses the existing `run_borrowed` spawn door and explicit slot-3 mapping, environment annotation, git auto-gc/maintenance disabling, driver preparation and release rule. It introduces no additional containment backend or suspended-start barrier. Predecessor handling stays unchanged: Linux borrows declare no new predecessor record and clean up the borrowed child's process group and descendants; macOS uses the child's process group. Git Publication disables hooks in its own driver before calling this port, as Git spec §10 rule 4a requires.

Exceeding either byte ceiling returns `borrow-output-limit: stdout|stderr`; reaching the deadline returns `borrow-deadline`. On either refusal, or an I/O failure (`borrow-io-failed`), the root is killed, waited without reaping, the existing borrow domain's leftovers are ended, and the root is reaped before returning. The handle remains owned by the caller throughout. Remaining output is drained after normal root exit and leftover cleanup. As with `run_borrowed`, failure to end leftovers takes precedence and returns `borrow-leftover-not-killed`; this is never a successful empty-domain claim. Windows refuses this new form with `borrow-io-unsupported` before any child is started; its existing job-backed `run_borrowed` is unchanged.

Clarified 2026-10-18 (refined): every acquire opens its own description. Outside a borrow, only the holder and its direct children between fork and exec can hold that description; it is close-on-exec everywhere else. On Linux drain, holders in the borrowed child's process group or descended from it are killed. A holder that is a direct child of the holder process and outside the borrow group is a pre-exec child: wait bounded by `killWaitMs` and re-check the description, never kill it. Any other holder of the description can only be an escaped descendant of a borrowed child, is inside the borrow's authority, and is killed, then drained and verified. Signals pin and re-check process identity. The Node fd facade routes drain through the Rust `lock-fd --drain-child` helper, passing the held description explicitly; the helper excludes itself and its parent (the holder) and applies this same rule. Unix borrowed children remain leaders of their own process groups. Non-spawning `validate_quiescent(&Handle)` has no borrow kill authority: it waits bounded and refuses unresolved holders before Publication writes Intent or supersession. A timeout or unprovable drain retains the held handle and exclusion; it never claims empty.

Clarified 2026-10-19: a narrowed per-spawn `Reach::Since` pass assumes that copies are inherited by fork, ordinary cyclic PID allocation is used (no privileged `clone3(set_tid)` or `ns_last_pid` override), and allocation stays below 4,000,000 PIDs/s inside the `pid_max / 4,000,000` window. An old or unreadable allocation mark falls back to start-time filtering over the process table. Descriptor transfers by `SCM_RIGHTS` or `pidfd_getfd` to pre-existing processes are outside that narrowed candidate set. The floor lags by one successful proof: proof N advances it only to the start of proof N-1, so a fork in flight at proof N remains eligible at N+1. Failed and out-of-order proofs do not advance it.

A positive tagged record, blocked probe or any uncertainty enters the full tagged descriptor scan. Holders of this inode whose FLOCK record stamps this process are signalled by an identity captured before scanning their descriptors and pinned again at signal time, except direct children (pre-exec copies: waited, never killed). A live own handle, or a positive record of a later acquirer, proves the old EX description gone by exclusivity and spares that acquirer and its borrowers. Recheck own handles before each signal; no kcmp is necessary once the own-handle proof holds. An empty scan alone does not prove release across an in-flight fork: repeat table/probe/scan until positively proven or `killWaitMs` passes, returning `lock-release-stuck` with killed count and remaining pids. A dropped handle runs the same settle; `release` returns its outcome. Descriptor transfer to a pre-existing process is found at release, not borrow return: such a recipient runs until release, at most the length of the hold. Shared handles close directly. The Node facade's unknown-history `lock-fd --drain-child` keeps reading every process.

The opaque addon handover protects acquired handles from request-data forgery; it is not an isolation boundary against arbitrary code already executing inside the Node process. The first-caller registration capability is per Node worker thread. Code that loads the native addon before the trusted facade can consume that capability and deny facade startup (fail closed). A hostile module or worker thread therefore requires process isolation; possession of request data, a path or an fd number never grants a holder handle. Native borrowed copies remain close-only and are drained before the facade borrow guard releases.

## 8. The predecessor domain rule

0. **Release rule (custody extension, 2026-10-18).** The holder clears only its own unchanged predecessor record with `clear_domain(handle)` after observing its domain empty, while still holding exclusion, then closes. Execution does this after the runner commit receipt and persisted handoff. An absent record means a recorded handoff or that no producer ran. An unknown launch or unproven domain leaves the record for successor admission. `clear_domain` never kills a domain. **Limitation (owner decision 2026-10-19):** for a best-effort domain kind (`linux-pgroup`, `macos-tree`) "observed empty" sees the process group or tree only, so a `setsid` or double-fork escapee is not seen and a recorded handoff over such a domain does not cover it; admission after a controller death still refuses these kinds. On supervised Linux the attempt gate is a subreaper and kills adopted escapees before the receipt, so the exposure is unconfined Linux and macOS. Revisit when containment drivers give those platforms a provable domain.

**Borrow cleanup.** Cleanup covers the borrowed child's process group, descendants and escaped description holders under §5's refined 2026-10-18 rule. Only direct pre-exec children of the holder outside the borrow group are waited, never killed. Hook-enabled borrows (including checkpoint and merge commits) still kill setsid/double-fork escapees holding the description; ancestry loss does not spare an escapee. A holder releases only after `run_borrowed` has waited for the child, killed leftovers in its authority, drained and verified empty. A non-empty predecessor domain found after the next holder took the lock means the previous holder died abnormally. On Linux the holder's own release settles against the kernel lock table as §5 describes; the next holder's predecessor rule is unchanged.

1. A holder that will create a process domain while it holds the lock (a job for `run_borrowed` on Windows; the attempt's namespace or job) writes `<lockFile>.predecessor.json` right after acquire and before creating the domain, while it still holds the lock: `{v: 1, domainKind, domainId}`. `domainKind` is `linux-pgroup` (best-effort), `linux-gate` (the gate's process tuple; empty iff `judge(tuple) == dead`), `windows-job` (a named Job Object) or `macos-tree` (a tree root tuple; best-effort). The record is written through a temp file and a rename. A missing record means the holder handed off after proving empty, or created no domain.

2. The next holder, after it holds the kernel lock, reads the record and asks the driver whether the domain is empty. Empty, or unopenable but proven empty: proceed. Not empty: kill the whole domain at once; never wait for it to drain.

3. Then wait at most `killWaitMs` (`lock.predecessorKillWaitMs`, default 2000 ms; measured a few ms) for the killed processes to be signaled. Domain empty: proceed. Deadline passed, or the kill was refused: release the kernel lock and return `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)` naming the domain; doctor shows that domain.

5. A holder that proceeded and will create a domain itself overwrites the record before creating it. A record with `v != 1`, or an unreadable record, is never deleted or ignored: acquire returns `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)` with the raw record.

Why kill at once rather than wait for the domain to drain: a drain only helps a holder that was allowed to leave processes running after release, and step 0 forbids that. The second Windows measurement showed every contender waiting the full 2000 ms before terminating; killing at once brings the crash path down to a few milliseconds (p50 5.9 ms, p95 6.9 ms over 50 runs). A holder that violates step 0 on purpose has its leftover killed by the next holder: that is the holder's defect, and `lock-borrow-vectors` catches the known vectors.

`linux-gate` is judged by `judge(gate) == dead` and ended by SIGKILL by identity. On Linux `run_borrowed` declares no predecessor record; it kills the borrowed child's process group, descendants and escaped description holders under §5's refined rule, each signaled by identity. Direct pre-exec children of the holder outside the borrow group are waited and re-checked, never killed. Domain cleanup fails with a named error `borrow-leftover-not-killed` and the pid when one survives the deadline. On macOS the leftovers are the child's process group. `macos-tree` stays contract only until the run supervisor's macOS containment lands. `windows-job` is implemented, as section 8.1 says.

- **Record shape.** `domainKind: windows-job`, `domainId = {job, sessionId, declaredAt, holder: {host, pid, startTime}, keeper: {host, pid, startTime} | null}`, `v` stays 1. `declaredAt` and `startTime` are decimal FILETIME strings; `keeper` is filled by rewriting the record right after the keeper's ack, before any member exists. A string `domainId` parses to nothing, so it stays fail closed.

- **Two views of the domain.** The **job view** (release rule and keeper): `ActiveProcesses == 0` and every member named by the job's pid list or by a Toolhelp scan for `IsProcessInJob` is signaled. The **contender view** (`admit`, after the kernel lock is held): a live recorded holder released normally, so the job view decides and only `TerminateJobObject` ever runs; a dead holder gives the union of the job list, the in-job scan and the holder's descendants created at or after `declaredAt` (minus the keeper), re-read on every poll. A pid that is live but cannot be opened keeps the domain not empty. A job that does not open falls back to the tree source with two consecutive quiet snapshots. In that fallback, a process created at or after `declaredAt` whose parent has left the snapshot (or whose pid now belongs to a newer process), and its descendants, are also waited for, for 200 ms after the job was first found gone (a one-shot window; nothing new is named after it closes): a member of a closed job whose parent already exited is no longer reachable from the holder and is still tearing down (measured on Windows CI: a live git pid named by no source, one in about 150 rounds). A holder pid that now belongs to a newer process ends the clause (the holder died a while ago, nothing is tearing down). The 200 ms window is a timing assumption: a member whose teardown outlasts it and that no other source names could still slip, and the owner's 500-repeat gate is the test for it. They are only waited for, never signaled, because an unrelated orphan looks the same. A record of another session is `NotEmpty` with reason `predecessor-other-session`. The contract is [`predecessor.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/predecessor.v1.json) `windowsJobViews`.

- **Doctor.** `lock-holders` judges a `windows-job` record with the read-only `fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state <lockFile>` (one contender-view pass, never kills): `empty` and `absent` are fine, `not-empty` and `unknown` warn with the domain and the reason (for example `predecessor-other-session`). `linux-gate` and `macos-tree` records keep the Node `judge()` path.
- `held` with reason `predecessor-domain-not-empty` becomes the named error `lock-predecessor-domain-not-empty` with the domain; `borrow-leftover-not-killed` keeps its name.

The routes live in `apps/fgos/src/main.rs` as the earliest branch of `main()` (before any composition, provider or spawn, so no child can inherit fd 3). They are not in `command-routes.json` and not in help. Every route requires `--protocol 1`; absent or different, the answer is `host-version-mismatch` (one release, one protocol). Each prints one JSON line on stdout (`{v: 1, protocol: 1, ...}`); stderr is for people and never parsed.

The Git-WAL activation fence is placed by the **new fgctl**, inside its activation critical section, rather than by doctor. It holds `activation-v2.lock` and the old `activation.lock`; the first `git-wal-v1` activation atomically exchanges the held old file for a prepared directory carrying `{lock: "activation", at: <ISO timestamp>, by: "fgos git"}` in `TOMBSTONE`, then syncs the parent. An old controller sees the held inode or `EISDIR`, never an unfenced interval. Linux uses `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)`; platforms without this primitive refuse placement. Node fence placement leaves this path to fgctl, while fence status still reports it: `fenceStatus` lists it in `targets` and, while unfenced, in `controllerMissing`, never in `missing`, `v1Present` or `complete`, which cover only the fences Node places; doctor reports `git-fence-missing` once every Node fence is in place and this one is not. The original 4.4 installation-path fence remains. Rollback retains the fence.
The fences that remain are the cheapest thing that makes an old binary fail loudly rather than hold a legacy lock beside a kernel lock:

| `lock-holders` | The kernel's holder list for every existing lock file of this track's registry rows (run and account rows enumerated from their directories) | A holder warns with pid and cmdline unless it is a borrowed child of that lock (`FGOS_LOCK_FD=<name>:<slot>` in its environment), a process the host started (the `FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pin), or a fgOS payload by argv (`fgos`, `fgos-runner`, `fgos-gateway`, `bin/fgos.mjs`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`). A `<lock>.predecessor.json` whose domain is not judged dead, whose version is unknown, or which names a Windows job the host does not judge empty warns with the domain and the reason; a record written in another PID namespace judges `unknown` and keeps warning (and keeps the lock `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)`) until a person confirms the domain is gone and removes the record. Holders that cannot be listed are informational |

The main checkout is written by claim, merge, land and the `.fgos` checkpoint. Its single guard is the `main-checkout` mutex (rank 50, `<fgosDir>/locks/main-checkout.lock`, [registry](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json)): a kernel lock like every other mutex, so it has no TTL, no ambiguous state, no recognition of a holder by pid and no protocol marker. The kernel answers `held` or `free`; nothing in the component decides anything from a pid or a clock.

**One door.** Code reaches the main checkout through `withMainCheckout(scope, purpose, fn)`, which acquires the mutex in the caller's `LockScope` (section 9) and hands `fn` a `mainHandle`. A function that must write under the lock (the `.fgos` checkpoint) takes the handle as a required argument and never acquires by itself. A caller that already holds main (claim) passes its handle down; a merge holds only its slot while it merges and verifies in a temporary worktree, and calls `withMainCheckout` just for the checkpoint, the merge commit and the land. The order in a scope is fixed by rank: merge slot 20, `worktree-admin` 40, main checkout 50 (the state store locks sit at 60 in the registry).

**The merge slot** is a mutex per target ref (rank 20), at `<fgosDir>/locks/merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>.lock`; the encoded ref is what v1 already wrote. It serialises merges into one ref and is released after the merge, after main.

**Borrowing replaces `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`.** The holder runs every git child of a checkpoint or merge through `runBorrowed` (section 3), which gives the locked description to exactly that child in slot 3 with `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` and prepends `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/main-checkout-borrow.v1.json)). The `.githooks/pre-commit` hook, which git runs inside that child, is a borrower only when the three conditions of section 5 hold, checked by `fgos internal lock-fd --protocol 1 --borrowed-check <lock path>`. A borrower skips the activity beacon, because the lock proves who is committing. Anything else is a stranger: the hook probes `main-checkout` once with a description of its own, refuses when it is held, and never waits (git already holds `index.lock`, rank 55). The child cannot release the lock for the holder, cannot pass the description on beyond git's own hooks and cannot start anything in the background; the holder waits for the child before the transaction counts as done. The worker base env of a dispatch drops `FGOS_LOCK_FD`; a leaked variable gives nothing without the description.

**Critical section rules, thrown at once.** The callback is synchronous; a thenable result throws `state-tx-async`. Starting a child process inside the section (any `child_process` export, including named ESM imports) throws `exec-under-hot-lock` at the call; acquiring a hot mutex again in the same process throws `hot-lock-reentry` without waiting. Values that need git or the host (`mainFgosDir`, `head`, the writer identity) are read before the lock and passed in as `prefetched`. There is no switch that turns the guard off.

**Lock order.** Hot mutexes sit at rank 60, above the main checkout (50): a claim reads HEAD, takes the `state` transaction for the check and the claim record, and takes main only around the `.fgos` checkpoint, never inside the state transaction.

Nothing in the repo-lock core (sections 14, 16) imports the event log, a shard or `withStateTx`; the `.fgos` checkpoint of the main door stays a detachable adapter. The event file format, `merge=union`, `.gitattributes` and the `.fgos` strip rule are untouched: they belong to the event store cutover ([event store spec](../event-store/spec.md) section 13 names `withStateTx` as the Work gate).

`worktree-admin` is a mutex (rank 40, `<fgosDir>/locks/worktree-admin.lock`) with no v1 predecessor and no fence. It wraps every fgOS call of `git worktree add`, `git worktree remove`, `git worktree move` (relocate) and `git worktree prune`. For remove and relocate, the dirty-check of the worktree, the destroy or move, and the registration change run under one hold of the lock, so no other worktree administration can run between the check and the effect (Git lessons G-042, G-155). It stays one lock: there is no second admin lock, and read-only listing takes none. Rank 40 is below main checkout (50), so no wrapped worktree command runs while main is held: a claim creates its worktree after it has released main; a merge creates its temporary worktree under the merge slot (20), before it takes main.

A best-effort `linux-pgroup` or `macos-tree` record cannot prove successor custody after controller death; Execution refuses that worktree even when the group appears empty. A crash while a borrow runs on Windows costs the next acquire about 120-170 ms.

Until Git phase 03 owns removal/recovery, preserve the refused checkout and use a fresh worktree. To recover that same checkout manually: stop all dispatchers for it, identify the exact lock path in the refusal, inspect its `.predecessor.json` with `fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state <lock-path>`, fence the recorded producer and every possible descendant (including escaped sessions), and verify no writer remains. Only under that quiescence may an operator archive/remove that **predecessor record**; retain the lock file itself. An empty group or a free kernel lock alone does not authorize this action. Unprovable process membership means keep the record and use the replacement tree. Do not automate record deletion by age or PID liveness.

Cold process startup (runtime init, imports, configuration, protocol negotiation) is materially more expensive than talking to an already-running provider — acceptable for a coarse, infrequent operation, not for thousands of helper-sized calls. A persistent stdio connection or local socket removes repeated startup cost, but serialization, scheduling, and backpressure remain, so ports expose complete use-case operations and batch hot loops behind one request. For a normal one-shot CLI invocation, keeping a plugin process alive beyond the host lifetime adds daemon lifecycle without necessarily saving work; persistence is justified for the remote host, interactive sessions, or one invocation making repeated provider calls.

The cost is temporary: a legacy CLI call pays both the small Rust launcher and Node startup, distribution must ship both runtimes, and compatibility failures can occur before any command becomes faster. The architecture only pays off if the first Rust host remains thin and forwards legacy behavior rather than rewriting every parser and use case at once.

- Lookup, by name, first match wins: the workspace folder, then a domain or extension (`domains/<name>/agents/`), then the installed `core/agents`. A higher tier replaces the whole file of a lower one; fields are never merged. Two definitions of one name in the same tier are an error that `fgos doctor` reports, never a silent pick. - **The main checkout.** `fgctl` checks the main checkout with `probe` (shared, non-blocking, never held) on `<fgosDir>/locks/main-checkout.lock` and nothing else: a held lock refuses `init`, `upgrade` and `repair`; the old `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` (file or tombstone directory) is never read, so there is no ttl, stale or ambiguous answer. 2026-10-17: the v1 read this bullet used to carry went away with the main checkout cutover.

- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.

Specified by RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder) but not built yet: the `fgctl init` skeleton and README, and routing the unit-level and capability-level `persona:` names through the same three-tier lookup (only `--seats @name` uses it today; those names are still read from `core/agents` of the working project in `renderPersonaSection`, `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`). How an extension declares its root is undefined: no extension loader exists, only the domain layer.

**Guarantee level.** `kernel` means the OS itself keeps the domain: a PID namespace, a Job Object. `best-effort` means the driver finds and kills what it can see; on a best-effort platform a free attempt lock does not prove that no writer remains, so adopt waits and scans again, and the attempt's binding records the level. No platform is refused for being best-effort; the level is said out loud (doctor `process-containment`, `fgos run --json`, `dispatch inspect`).

1. *Reused pgid.* On `macos-tree` and on `linux-pgroup` (best-effort), a pgid scan made after the leader died can meet a pgid the kernel has since given to an unrelated group. The drivers signal a group only while the leader still matches its recorded identity and otherwise fall back to the descendant list gathered earlier; a window remains where a scan after the leader's death cannot tell a stranger's group from the domain's.

Domain primitives of section 4 are what the port uses underneath: `linux-gate` and `windows-job` and `macos-tree` records are judged by `domain_is_empty` / `domain_kill_all` or their watchers; `linux-pgroup` is a `domainKind` of the predecessor record.

- **2026-10-18 — Fast-exit containment:** Successful spawn remains successful when the child exits before identity capture. Linux process-group and macOS tree roots retain an unreaped child's start time, including zombies; group members still determine emptiness. A bwrap `child-pid` reported under `--unshare-pid --as-pid-1` names namespace init: if already absent, its `linux-gate` tuple carries reserved start time `exited-before-identity`, an empty-domain tombstone whose kill is a no-op (including record-only checks); the monitor still yields the actual exit status. Missing namespace reports remain `namespace-unavailable`, and unreadable identity is never evidence of emptiness.
